pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher - Westwood with Iford Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to Westwood with Iford primary school. We are proud to be the Head of School and Executive Headteacher of this vibrant village school. As you look through our website, you will see a little of everything that the school has to offer. We hope this will give you a glimpse of what your child(ren) will experience through their school life with us.
Our Ofsted Report (May 2025) judged us to be Good in all areas. This reflects the hard work of our staff, pupils and school community and the caring nature of our school. We urge you to come and see the jewel nestled in the village of Westwood, just outside of Trowbridge. We are really looking forward to meeting you and showing you around our amazing school.
We believe in ensuring that children receive a well-rounded curriculum that provides opportunities to develop characteristics for effective learning and life in all its fullness, whilst enabling children’s passion for learning to flourish.
Our family feel with a high staff ratio mean that children’s individual talents can be spotted and nurtured enabling everyone to experience success and reach their full potential. The children benefit from a dedicated staff team who work tirelessly to ensure that the children reach high standards whilst feeling happy and supported because we believe that happy children achieve more!
We firmly believe that education is a partnership between home and school with you being an active partner in your child’s education. This successful relationship with parents, the local community and the other schools within Palladian Academy Trust, means that we can continue to ‘Inspire success in a world of possibilities’.
Heather Saunders - Head of School
Simon Futcher - Executive Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Values and Ethos - Westwood with Iford Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our Values and Ethos
Our Values and Ethos
twitterTweet this page
Our Values and Ethos
Inspiring success in a world of possibilities
In our school we aim to:
Encourage all pupils to develop their self-motivation, esteem and self-discipline and their independence.
Create a learning environment where children are happy to take risks and are able to accept the challenge of Life Long Learning, and are enabled to achieve their best.
Encourage a responsible and caring attitude to other people and the environment.
Offer an environment in which pupils are able to express their ideas and emotions confidently and can respond successfully and adapt to change.
Ensure that all pupils are treated equally and helped to develop tolerance and respect for others irrespective of their ability, ethnicity, gender, creed or need.
Foster and develop a close and co-operative relationship between school and parents, and school and the community.
We bring this to life by creating a stimulating, learning environment where the children are happy to take risks, and engage in their own learning. We are fortunate to have extensive grounds with a pond and a forest schools area. We are excited that we have been able to bring Forest Schools into the week enabling the children to move their learning beyond the physical classroom.
Our nurturing approach means that every child is successful. We focus on ensuring that their emotional wellbeing is positive as this enables them to build long lasting relationships with others and the world around them as well as being able to take risks in their learning.
The opportunities and learning experiences that our children have during their time at Westwood, ensure that they leave school feeling confident and prepared for their next phase of education.
Our children's results show we are consistently above national averages. We achieve this in part by seeing Westwood as OUR school. We are a thriving local school, at the heart of a small village, and we use this to our advantage. You only need to come and visit to see this for yourself.
Our School Values Are:
Curiosity: To ask questions and explore
Kindness: Be kind and helpful
Resilience: Keep trying and don't give up
Respect: Treat others the way that you want to be treated
We use the Thrive approach to promote positive mental health and emotional wellbeing in children and young people. Support for mental health and wellbeing in schools | The Thrive Approach

Westwood with Iford is committed to providing high quality physical education for all its pupils. Both the provision and impact of the sports premium can be seen by reading the information below.

pageCache.pageTitle: Governors - Westwood with Iford Primary School
pageCache.text:
Governors
The Governing Body exists to provide strategic oversight to the way the school is run and to be accountable for the decisions made by it. We have one over-riding purpose: to help make Westwood with Iford the best place for our children to learn.
On 1st October 2019 Fitzmaurice Primary School became part of Palladian Academy Trust. In January 2022 the Trust started working with Westwood with Iford Primary School who formally joined the Trust on 1st July 2022.
Please click here to see the governance structures of the trust:
https://www.palladianacademytrust.com/20/executive-and-non-executive-governance
The Trust Board convenes Local Governance Committees, which work with specific schools and have delegated responsibilities from the Trust Board, in order to ensure the non-executive of the Trust fulfils the three core purposes of governance which are:
ensuring clarity of vision, ethos and strategic direction
holding executive leaders to account for the educational performance of the organisation and its pupils, and the effective and efficient performance management of staff; and
overseeing the financial performance of the organisation and making sure its money is well spent.
The Local Governance Committee (LGC) also has a role in engaging with all stakeholders in the school(s) and wider community.
As Westwood with Iford Primary School (WWI) and Fitzmaurice Primary School (FPS) have a shared executive leadership structure, in order to ensure joined up decision-making and that all the relevant context is taken into account to make the best provision for the children, from February 2023 the LGCs from the two schools combined into a single committee, with responsibility for both schools.
The Chair of the FPSWWI LGC is Andrew Pilsworth.
Schools are required to publish the following information regarding their governors:
For a full list of governors click here
For a list of relevant business interests of governors 2023-24 please click here
Throughout the year we have responsibility for ensuring statutory compliance in Health and Safety, Safeguarding, monitoring academic progress, and recruiting teaching staff amongst many other things.
The School Governing Body (local governing committee) meets once a term 6 times a year. Governors also meet with the School Leadership team and Palladian's CEO & COO.
Minutes for the School Governing Body meetings are available on request from:
m.joy@palladianacademytrust.com
Please note this mailbox is only monitored during term time.

pageCache.pageTitle: List of Governors - Westwood with Iford Primary School
pageCache.text:
List of Governors
Simon Futcher - Ex Officio - Executive Headteacher
I have the enormous privilege of being the Executive Headteacher across Fitzmaurice Primary School, Westwood with Iford Primary School and Churchfields, the Village School. All schools are proud members of Palladian Academy Trust.
I have worked in a number of schools and taught every primary age group from nursery to year six. Before taking up my current role in January 2024, I have had substantial successful experience as both a Headteacher and Deputy Headteacher of small village and large city schools.
I have also served as a governor in many schools for a period exceeding twenty years so am fully aware that the relationship between the governing body and leadership team is pivotal for ensuring the ongoing success of any school. This takes the form of the Local Governing Committee being a ‘critical friend’ to support yet challenge the leadership team to ensure we provide the best possible education for our pupils.
Helen Lewis, Vice Chair of Governors
Helen Lewis joined the Westwood with Iford Governing Team as a community Governor in 2018 and transitioned to the joint governing team when Westwood with Iford primary school joined Palladian Trust. She is the current Vice Chair and link Governor for Disadvantaged Learners. Having previously worked as European Supply Chain manager, she’s proof that you don’t have to have an educational background to contribute to the governance of your local primary school. Passionately believing that every child has the right to a fun, inspiring and high quality of education primary years, she’s committed to challenging the current operational team to ensure our community’s children leave school fully equipped to meet life’s challenges and achieve their dreams.
Liz Parry, Community Governor
Liz Parry has been a governor of Fitzmaurice Primary school since 2022 and Westwood with Iford since the Local Governing committee combined.
Liz has lived in Bradford on Avon for ten years and is a local General Practitioner and parent to three children who all attend Fitzmaurice Primary School.
Isabelle Duck, Parent Governor
Isabelle joined the Governing Body for Westwood with Iford and Fitzmaurice Primary School as a Parent Governor in January 2024, bringing valuable experience in education and a strong connection to our school community. A proud parent of a daughter who attends Westwood with Iford, Isabelle is thrilled that her daughter is the third generation of their family to be part of the school. This long-standing family tradition reflects the deep roots and special place the school holds in their hearts. With eight years of teaching experience, Isabelle now holds a leadership role at a nearby school. As a Parent Governor, Izzie is committed to supporting both schools, ensuring the best outcomes for all students, and upholding the values and traditions that make these schools truly special.
Fran Stevens, Parent Governor
Fran has a background in education, having worked as a secondary school teacher for twelve years, before having children. She joins the Governing Body for Weswood with Iford and Fiztmaurice Primary Schools as a Parent Governor, as her two children now attend Fitzmaurice Primary. Having moved to Bradford on Avon in 2017, Fran is passionate about cooking and food writing. She is a recipe writer for a Wiltshire-based magazine, as well as running her own food blog. More generally, she works as a copywriter.
Abigail Thorpe, Community Governor
Abigail is delighted to have joined as a Community Governor for Fitzmaurice and Westwood and Iford Primary schools. She has a daughter who attends Fitzmaurice Primary School and after a career as a Primary school teacher, she now works as a private tutor, teaching children online internationally. Abigail and her family have lived in local area for five years, following eight years in New Zealand.
Heather Saunders - Staff Governor - Head of School WWI
Heather is Head of School of Westwood with Iford School. She is the Designated Safeguarding Lead and SENCO. Heather is often accompanied by Hollie, the school dog who is a huge part of school life.
Jo Hill - Associate Governor - Head of School FPS
Jo has been working at Fitzmaurice since September 2012 as the Deputy Headteacher. She has been Head of School since September 2022. Jo has over 30 years teaching experience and has taught every primary age group from reception to year 6.
Alex Ladner, Staff Governor
Alex Ladner is new to the governor’s team, starting this year and joins as a staff member from Fitzmaurice school. He is in his third year of teaching at Fitzmaurice having recently passed his ECT last year.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum - Westwood with Iford Primary School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
At Westwood with Iford Primary School, children enjoy a broad and balanced curriculum that is designed to follow the EYFS framework and the National Curriculum through learning themes that are relevant to children's interests in fun and engaging way that enables them to learn the necessary knowledge and skills in order to be successful.
The children's learning is enhanced through a range of visits and visitors which bring their learning alive. Children have visited Longleat, the Bath Literature festival, and have met Steven Butler the author of the No Where Hotel series of books. Year 6 have been to Pencellli and Year 4 to Charterhouse on a residential visit.
When you visit our classes you will find the children engaged in learning that challenges their thinking whilst developing their confidence and independence. The curriculum is enhanced with the children engaging in Forest Schools and in Key Stage 2 learning to swim. Our children have the opportunity to participate in a choir and are going to 'Young Voices' again this year. Our Year 5 & 6 children have performed at the Wiltshire Music Centre with the Orchestra for the Age of Enlightenment. Year 3 learn to play the violin and they can continue with lessons should they wish to as they move through Key Stage 2. We have a music teacher who comes into school weekly when the children can learn the Piano or Recorder.
For more detail on what each individual class (or year group) is studying, please take a look at the relevant class page. If you require further information about our curriculum please contact your child’s class teacher or if you are a visitor to the site, please contact the school office.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Clubs - Westwood with Iford Primary School
pageCache.text:
School Clubs
We provide before and after school provision. Breakfast club runs daily from 7.45am and children enjoy having breakfast and calm activities to start the day.
Our after school club is 3.20-4.20pm. The sessions are run by IG Sport and staff, who offer a range of activities such as Archery, Arts and Crafts, Dance, Football and seasonal activities such as Christmas Club.
We also have a lunchtime choir who are currently learning all the songs for the 'Young Voices' concert!
